title: The text discusses the challenges faced by Nigerian football clubs in the Nigerian Professional Football League (NPFL). The league has been experiencing a decline in spectatorship and revenue, which has made it difficult for clubs to run smoothly. Many players move to Europe after scoring a few goals, which disrupts the rhythm of their clubs. The article suggests that there are several factors contributing to these problems, including the lack of stability in keeping players throughout the season and the decline in the standard of football displayed at league match venues. The article concludes by stating that the league needs to be examined and fine-tuned to improve its overall run.
